title: Three jars: a simple way to split any money that arrives
description: Envelope budgeting in its simplest form: when money arrives, split it on the spot into Spend, Save and Share. Why deciding once, in advance, beats deciding every time.

body.heading: Decide once, not every time
paragraphs: The three-jar method is the old envelope system shrunk to its bones. Money that arrives — wages, a gift, pocket money — is divided immediately into three containers: Spend for now, Save for later, Share for giving. The percentages are yours to choose; a common starting split is 70, 20 and 10.

The power is in the timing. Every spending decision made in a shop is a small battle between present-you and future-you. The jars settle the battle once, at the moment the money arrives, when nobody is hungry, rushed or being advertised at.

body.heading: Physical jars, digital jars
paragraphs: For children and beginners, real jars teach fastest: you can watch Save fill and feel Spend empty. For adults the same structure works as three bank accounts or three labelled pots in a banking app — what matters is that the split is visible and the transfer happens on arrival, not with whatever is left at the end of the month. Leftovers are a plan that rarely survives contact with a month.
Review the split twice a year. If Save is always raided, the split is wrong, not you: adjust the percentages until the system fits the life it is meant to serve.

takeaway: Split money on arrival into Spend, Save and Share — deciding once, calmly, instead of at every till — and review the percentages twice a year.
